flags.description: Compares grand total lifetime_orders across all customers.
flags.sql: select 'total' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_orders) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_orders) from reference_output) as reference_value

flags.description: Compares overall order-weighted average order value (sum revenue / sum orders) to catch averaging errors.

flags.description: Compares the simple mean of per-customer avg_order_supply_cost, ignoring nulls, across all customers.

flags.description: Checks for duplicate customer_id rows by comparing total rows minus distinct keys in each table.

flags.description: Counts customer_id keys present in reference but absent from model output.
flags.sql: with j as (select m.customer_id as m_id, r.customer_id as r_id from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id) select 'missing_in_model' as slice, cast(0 as bigint) as model_value, sum(case when m_id is null and r_id is not null then 1 else 0 end) as reference_value from j

flags.description: Counts customer_id keys present in model but absent from reference output.

flags.description: Compares lifetime_orders per customer, full outer joined on customer_id.

flags.description: Compares avg_order_value per customer, full outer joined on customer_id.

flags.description: Compares first_order_date per customer (as days since epoch) to catch date boundary or timezone truncation errors.

flags.description: Compares the count of customers whose last_order_date falls in the most recent calendar month in each table.

flags.description: Compares the count of customers with exactly one lifetime order, an edge case for avg_order_value calculation.
flags.sql: select 'single_order_customers_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where lifetime_orders = 1) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where lifetime_orders = 1) as reference_value

flags.description: Compares the mean avg_order_value among single-order customers, where avg_order_value should equal order_total.
flags.sql: select 'single_order_avg_order_value_mean' as slice, (select avg(avg_order_value) from model_output where lifetime_orders = 1) as model_value, (select avg(avg_order_value) from reference_output where lifetime_orders = 1) as reference_value

flags.description: Compares the count of customers with a null avg_order_supply_cost, testing the 'exclude orders with no item records rather than count as zero' rule.
flags.sql: select 'null_avg_order_supply_cost_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is null) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is null) as reference_value

flags.description: Checks internal consistency of each table by comparing the gap between summed lifetime_revenue and summed (avg_order_value * lifetime_orders).
flags.sql: select 'revenue_minus_avg_times_orders' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) - sum(avg_order_value * lifetime_orders) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) - sum(avg_order_value * lifetime_orders) from reference_output) as reference_value

flags.description: Compares the order-count-weighted average of avg_order_supply_cost across customers, distinct from the simple per-customer mean.
flags.sql: select 'total_weighted_supply_cost' as slice, (select sum(avg_order_supply_cost * lifetime_orders) / sum(lifetime_orders) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null) as model_value, (select sum(avg_order_supply_cost * lifetime_orders) / sum(lifetime_orders) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null) as reference_value

flags.description: Compares total lifetime_revenue grouped into lifetime_orders buckets (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+).
flags.sql: with mb as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from model_output group by 1), rb as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mb.bucket, rb.bucket) as slice, mb.rev as model_value, rb.rev as reference_value from mb full outer join rb on mb.bucket = rb.bucket

flags.description: Compares the count of customers grouped into lifetime_orders buckets (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+).
flags.sql: with mb as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, count(*) as cnt from model_output group by 1), rb as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, count(*) as cnt from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mb.bucket, rb.bucket) as slice, mb.cnt as model_value, rb.cnt as reference_value from mb full outer join rb on mb.bucket = rb.bucket

flags.description: Counts customer_id keys that match between tables but have differing customer_name values, expecting zero mismatches.
flags.sql: select 'name_mismatch_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output m join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id where m.customer_name <> r.customer_name) as model_value, cast(0 as bigint) as reference_value

flags.description: Compares lifetime_revenue for the top 10 customers by reference revenue, to verify high-value accounts are not distorted.
flags.sql: with top10 as (select customer_id from reference_output order by lifetime_revenue desc limit 10) select r.customer_id as slice, m.lifetime_revenue as model_value, r.lifetime_revenue as reference_value from reference_output r left join model_output m on m.customer_id = r.customer_id where r.customer_id in (select customer_id from top10)

ai.prompt:
A dbt model has been changed and must be reconciled against an independent reference dashboard before it ships.

## Model: customer_lifetime_value

### Business definition (from the model's YAML)
Lifetime value per customer. One row per real customer with at least one qualifying order (internal "QA Test Account" customers and refunded orders are excluded). lifetime_revenue is the sum of qualifying order totals including tax. avg_order_value is lifetime_revenue / lifetime_orders. avg_order_supply_cost is the mean supply cost over qualifying orders that have item records; orders with no item records are excluded from the average rather than counted as zero.

### Model SQL (dbt/Jinja, DuckDB dialect)
```sql
with

orders as (

    select * from {{ ref('orders') }}

),

customers as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_customers') }}

),

refunds as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_refunds') }}

),

qualifying_orders as (

    select
        orders.*,
        customers.customer_name

    from orders

    inner join customers
        on orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id

    left join refunds
        on orders.order_id = refunds.order_id

    where not customers.is_test_account

)

select
    qualifying_orders.customer_id,
    qualifying_orders.customer_name,
    cast(min(qualifying_orders.ordered_at_ts) as date) as first_order_date,
    cast(max(qualifying_orders.ordered_at_ts) as date) as last_order_date,
    cast(count(qualifying_orders.order_id) as bigint) as lifetime_orders,
    cast(sum(qualifying_orders.order_total) as decimal(18, 2)) as lifetime_revenue,
    cast(sum(qualifying_orders.order_total) as double)
        / count(qualifying_orders.order_id) as avg_order_value,
    cast(avg(qualifying_orders.order_cost) as double) as avg_order_supply_cost

from qualifying_orders

group by 1, 2
```

## Tables available to your queries
Your queries run in a sandbox that contains exactly two tables and nothing else:

`model_output`: the model's output.
  - customer_id: VARCHAR
  - customer_name: VARCHAR
  - first_order_date: DATE
  - last_order_date: DATE
  - lifetime_orders: BIGINT
  - lifetime_revenue: DECIMAL(18,2)
  - avg_order_value: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_supply_cost: DOUBLE

`reference_output`: the trusted reference dashboard, computed independently from raw data at the same grain.
  - customer_id: VARCHAR
  - customer_name: VARCHAR
  - first_order_date: DATE
  - last_order_date: DATE
  - lifetime_orders: BIGINT
  - lifetime_revenue: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_value: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_supply_cost: DOUBLE

Grain (one row per): customer_id

## Task
Write up to 40 reconciliation queries comparing `model_output` to `reference_output`. Choose slices that would expose wrong numbers that still pass schema checks and data tests, for example: grand totals of each measure; totals by each dimension and dimension member; each available time grain (day, week, month, as applicable); edge periods (first/last periods, period boundaries); row counts and key coverage (keys present in one table but not the other); and averages/ratios where nulls or join fan-out could distort them.

Each query MUST return exactly these columns:
- `slice` (varchar): a human-readable label for the row, e.g. 'total', '2025-03 | Brooklyn'
- `model_value` (numeric): the value computed from model_output
- `reference_value` (numeric): the same value computed from reference_output

A query may return one row (a total) or many rows (one per slice). Use a full outer join on the slice keys so that slices missing on either side appear, with NULL on the missing side. Do not compute differences yourself; the harness compares model_value to reference_value. Return at most 5000 rows per query.
